items.label: Vintage hobbies in the modern world
src: Vintage hobbies
in the modern world

As the world in which we live becomes more high-tech and life unfolds online, many young people have been turning to **less modern** hobbies in their free time. Recently, everything from <u>stamp collecting</u> to <u>gardening</u>, <u>playing bingo</u> to <u>baking</u> and <u>decorating cakes</u> has become popular again. The question is, why?

Some of the **most popular** hobbies are artistic ones, such as <u>drawing</u>, <u>painting</u> and <u>sculpture</u>. Perhaps the reason we are becoming **more interested** in these hobbies is because they take us away from our screens.

Home-based hobbies like baking, <u>sewing</u> and gardening are also more popular than they used to be. They are **cheaper** than many outdoor hobbies and also more tactile (connected with touch), something which is missing from our online worlds.

Young people are also collecting things more than they used to. Collecting things from the past such as stamps or postcards makes us think **more deeply** about how our world has changed and connects us with the past.
But what is the **best** thing about all these hobbies? You can still share everything you do on social media!

in the modern world

As the world in which we live becomes more high-tech and life unfolds online, many young people have been turning to less modern hobbies in their free time. Recently, everything from stamp collecting to gardening, playing bingo to baking and decorating cakes has become popular again. The question is, why?

Some of the most popular hobbies are artistic ones, such as drawing, painting and sculpture. Perhaps the reason we are becoming more interested in these hobbies is because they take us away from our screens.

Home-based hobbies like baking, sewing and gardening are also more popular than they used to be. They are cheaper than many outdoor hobbies and also more tactile (connected with touch), something which is missing from our online worlds.

Young people are also collecting things more than they used to. Collecting things from the past such as stamps or postcards makes us think more deeply about how our world has changed and connects us with the past.

But what is the best thing about all these hobbies? You can still share everything you do on social media!

**Sarah** Bonjour, moi, c’est Sarah. J’habite à Bruxelles depuis toujours. C’est une jolie ville, agréable, internationale, surtout dans le quartier des institutions européennes. J’habite à quelques minutes à pied de la Grand-Place, dans une petite rue. Mes voisins viennent des quatre coins de l’Europe : de Grèce, du Portugal, des Pays-Bas... Je prends le métro pour aller au lycée : c’est plus rapide et pratique que le bus.

**Fatima** Je m’appelle Fatima. Je viens de Paris, j’ai longtemps habité aux États-Unis et au Canada. Je suis arrivée à Bruxelles il y a deux ans. C’est vrai, Bruxelles n’est pas aussi grande que Paris, il n’y a pas autant d’attractions, mais c’est tout de même une capitale, active et accueillante. J’habite dans un quartier très tranquille. Il y a une belle ambiance, on peut faire de longues promenades et les gens discutent beaucoup. Le soir, c’est très animé surtout à côté du célèbre Manneken Pis.

**Léon** Moi, c’est Léon et je suis né ici. Pour mon travail, je voyage beaucoup : au Brésil, en Chine, et même en Ouzbékistan, mais je reste très attaché à Bruxelles. C’est une ville chaleureuse et dynamique ; et même si elle est moins grande que d’autres capitales, on s’amuse autant. Et on est moins stressé ! La ville offre beaucoup de surprises et d’émotions : on ne s’ennuie jamais !

items.label: Hygge
src: In 2017, the Danish word hygge was added to the Oxford English Dictionary. But what exactly is hygge?

**A warm atmosphere**Hygge (pronounced "hooga") is hard to explain. It is about taking a break from busy life. You can spend time with people you care about—or even alone—to relax and enjoy simple pleasures.

Hygge often happens in a tidy, calm space with soft lighting, like candles or lamps. Natural elements, such as wood, plants, or wool, and warm colors and textures make the space feel cozy. You can sit with blankets and pillows in a warm corner to feel comfortable.
**Comfort and relaxation**Hygge is also about wearing cozy clothes like sweaters, socks, or scarves. It is a time to slow down, rest, and feel calm.

This lifestyle usually includes hot drinks such as tea, coffee, and hot chocolate. People often enjoy homemade food like soup, bread, cakes, or cookies. You can share comfort meals with family or friends.

**Togetherness and relationships**Hygge is about spending time with family and friends in small gatherings. You can share stories, laughter, or simple activities together. There is no strict plan—you just enjoy each other’s company.

**Mindset and feelings**Hygge is about enjoying the present moment, feeling safe, calm, and at home, and being grateful for small things. It is a way of life where people choose simplicity rather than stress or luxury.

**Why is hygge part of Danish life?**The cold, dark, and rainy weather in Denmark makes people spend time indoors. Fall and winter are the main time for hygge. Hygge also shows important Danish values: well-being for everyone. People avoid arguments to keep a positive atmosphere.
Sometimes hygge can be hard for outsiders. It usually happens in close, familiar groups, and new people may feel left out.
Adapted from: https://denmark.dk/people-and-culture/hygge

items.label: Raya’s podcast
src: Listen to Raya’s podcast and choose the best title
A. How to Make Your Home Cozy and Comfortable
B. Tips for Cooking Scandinavian Food
C. How to Read More Books at Home
D. How to Buy Antique Furniture
Hi, it’s Raya! Today I want to tell you about **10 ways to make your home cozy**.
First, you can make a small corner for reading. Put a comfortable chair or a sofa, some warm blankets, and good light. Keep books nearby. This is a nice place to relax.
Candles are also very good. They make your room warm and calm. You can light them in the evening. They give a cozy feeling for everyone.
If you have a fireplace, it is perfect for cozy evenings. If not, you can use a small fire outside, like a fire pit. It makes time with friends or family very comfortable.
The wood is nice and warm. You can use wooden tables, chairs, bowls, or decorations. Wood makes your home feel natural and cozy.
Bring some plants, flowers, or small pieces of nature inside. You can put pumpkins, pine cones, or leaves in your home. Nature makes the room fresh and cozy.
Keep books in your home. You can read them in your reading corner or look at them on the table. Books make your home interesting and relaxing.
Use cups, mugs, and plates that you like. Holding your favourite mug makes drinking tea or cocoa special and cozy.
Use soft blankets, cushions, or rugs. Different textures make your home comfortable.
Old furniture, small decorations, or antiques give a special feeling. They make your home unique and warm.
Finally, keep soft blankets and cushions everywhere. You can sit or lie down with them. This is one of the easiest ways to feel cozy.
Try these ideas and enjoy a comfortable, happy home!
